newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent triangle flags continuation.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent triangle flags continuation.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* An expanding triangle formation on the August chart is a continuation pattern but with a bearish undertone.
* The market looks bullish in the short term. But unless it can get up to $19 analysts see it pulling back sharply again.
IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures remain bullish in the short term but analysts are eyeing upside targets for confirmation that the current trends can be sustained.

Analysts said a supportive gap-up on the spot Brent chart between $18.18 Friday's close and $18.34 a barrel Monday's opening remained intact while a bullish cross of the 10/20-day moving averages also pointed the market towards fresh upside targets.

They said the next short term target would then be $19 which marks a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement then in the longer term the congested period in the $19.20-70 region on the August chart could be a target although new contract highs above $20.50 could take some time to achieve.

Independent Analyst Elli Gifford said an expanding triangle formation on the August chart was a continuation pattern but with a bearish undertone though she said there was very little to be bearish about at the moment.
"$17.94 is critical support, if this holds the aim would be in the $18.75 to $19 region where there is quite a lot of resistance," Gifford said.
"The market looks bullish in the short term. But unless it can get up to $19 the chances are we may see it pulling back sharply again," she added.
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said " The technical picture of the market is still neutral to negative, although we've seen Brent cover its selling extreme and build volume at higher levels".
Monday's price gains saw gas oil on spot month continuation chart in the middle of a third wave up, the previous two of which have peaked in the high $170s, $179.50 being the high of May 22.
However, analysts said Monday's narrow trading range of $1 could suggest some uncertainty as to the markets conviction to go higher.

Looking further out Elli Gifford said "$165.75 (on the August chart)from Friday's gap up is critical support, but a lot of resistance will be met around $167.25 which is the top of the gap down earlier this month".
August Brent on SIMEX was trading around $18.55 per barrel.
August NYMEX crude on ACCESS was last traded at $19.81, up one cent from the New York close. The contract had gained 34 cents a barrel to settle at $19.80 after rising as high as $19.90.
Brokers said prompt NYMEX crude broke technical resistance created by the session high on June 25 of $19.75. That level was the highest point for spot crude since June 6.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
